messages.author: 3f2c9ebed047db91
messages.subject: Fix ranges at nodes
parts:
Dear all

I'm dealing with a phylogeny consisting of 87 extant lineages and I would like to test alternative scenarios by constraining ranges at the root of the tree. I subdivided the geographical distribution of my group of study into 9 areas and set the max_range_size to 4. I tried to use the fixnode/fixlikes parameters as follows: fixnode = c(88) and fixlikes = c(1,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0) but I couldn't manage to restrict the root's node to the first defined area. Instead, BioGeoBEARS assigns a different geographical range to the root, based on what I see in the output after running the program.

Please let me know if I'm doing something wrong. I just assumed that the settings in BioGeoBEARS would be the same (or similar) to Lagrange, in which I used the option: fixnode = mrcaname distribution (i.e. for 9 defined areas, fixnode = ROOT 100000000).

Thanks a lot

Pavel

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Fix ranges at nodes
parts: Hi! I'm traveling, but the fixnode should be the node number in APE, and fix likes is for states not areas. If you have 2 areas, you have 4 possible states, null, a, b, or ab. To force the node to be ab you have fix likes be c(0,0,0,1). Cheers! Nick

messages.author: 3f2c9ebed047db91
messages.subject: Re: Fix ranges at nodes
parts:
Hi

Thanks a lot Nick, I managed to fix the root of the tree to alternative ranges. Since I had 9 areas and max_range_size=4, I had to add a vector with 256 states to the fixlikes option.

Cheers
